selected_mechanism.name: AS 38.05.810 'public and charitable use' noncompetitive conveyance of ~19,950 acres to AIDEA (ADL 234762, Houston Industrial Park)
selected_mechanism.one_line_definition: A DNR commissioner's discretionary written finding converts ~19,950 acres of sovereign state land into a noncompetitive fee conveyance to a state development authority under a statute whose eligible use is expressly 'not commercial development' — with the reversionary interest that normally polices that restriction waivable by the same officer.

news_trigger.verbatim_quote: There is no committed data center tenant, industrial developer, site plan, power source, cooling system, water supply plan or construction schedule.
news_trigger.outlet: Anchorage Daily News (opinion, by Brandon Brefczynski, Deputy Director, AIDEA)

layers.layer_name: L1 — Statutory disposal authority and the reversionary-interest waiver
layers.what_it_does: Authorizes noncompetitive disposal of state land for 'public and charitable use,' restricts eligible projects to uses that are 'not commercial development,' mandates a reversionary interest, and then permits that same interest to be waived by written public-interest determination.
layers.controlling_actor: Commissioner, Alaska Department of Natural Resources
layers.verified_quote_or_fact: Section title is 'Public and charitable use.' Subsection (c) contains the phrase 'not commercial development.' Subsection (g): 'The commissioner shall retain a reversionary interest on each sale or other disposal granted under (a) or (e) of this section. The commissioner may waive the reversionary interest on a written determination that the waiver is in the public interest.' Subsection (c) eligible applicants are 'nonprofit corporations, associations, clubs, or societies organized and operated exclusively for charitable, religious, scientific, or educational purposes, or for the promotion of social welfare.'

layers.layer_name: L2 — DMLW preliminary decision, comment window, and the appeal-standing filter
layers.what_it_does: Publishes the preliminary decision, area plan amendment, land classification order and mineral order; runs the comment period; and converts the preliminary decision into the Final Finding and Decision if no significant change is required. The comment period simultaneously determines who is ever permitted to appeal.
layers.controlling_actor: DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water, Land Sales & Contracts section (adjudication contact of record: Daniel Jenkins, 907-269-8609)
layers.verified_quote_or_fact: ADL 234762; 'approximately 19,950 acres'; recipient 'Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority (AIDEA)'; described as a 'noncompetitive public and charitable use conveyance'; notice published 7/10/2026; comment deadline '5:00 PM, Wednesday, August 19, 2026'; 'Only persons from whom DNR DMLW LCS receives timely, written comment during the identified comment period will be eligible to file an appeal'; 'If no significant change is required, the Preliminary Decision and related actions...will be issued as the Final Finding and Decision.'
layers.verification_caveat: The preliminary decision PDF (1.1MB) could not be text-extracted. The AS 38.05.810 basis is established by attachment filenames ('AIDEA_.810_Application_Complete_R.pdf', 'Houston Industrial Park .810 Decision-PD.pdf') plus the notice's use of the statute's exact term of art; the notice body itself cites only the AS 38.05.945 notice provision. The signing officer for the Final Finding and Decision is NOT identified on the notice. The words 'reversionary interest' and 'data center' do NOT appear in the notice.

layers.layer_name: L3 — Grantee as master developer, lessor and bond issuer
layers.what_it_does: Receives the land and holds independent statutory power to lease it on self-determined terms, take equity interests in projects, and issue bonds against them — i.e. to conduct the commercial development the conveying statute's eligible-use clause excludes.
layers.controlling_actor: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority (Executive Director Randy Ruaro; Deputy Director Brandon Brefczynski), acting under AS 44.88.080
layers.verified_quote_or_fact: Section title 'Powers of the authority.' Includes power 'to lease to others a project acquired by it for the rentals and upon the terms and conditions the authority may consider advisable'; 'to acquire an interest in a project as necessary or appropriate to provide financing for the project, whether by purchase, gift, or lease'; and 'to issue bonds and otherwise to incur indebtedness...in order to pay the cost of a project or development projects.' Confirmed independently: the 32 enumerated powers do NOT include authority to create subsidiaries.

chokepoint.actor: Commissioner, Alaska Department of Natural Resources
chokepoint.binary_decision: Two binaries owned by one officer: (1) sign or refuse to sign a finding that conveying ~19,950 acres to a bonding development authority for an industrial park is a 'public and charitable use' under a statute whose eligible-use clause reads 'not commercial development'; and (2) retain or waive the reversionary interest on a written determination that waiver 'is in the public interest.'
chokepoint.why_asymmetric: The statute assigns both decisions to 'the commissioner' singular — no board, no vote, no scored evaluation, no competitive process, and no statutory standard beyond the commissioner's own public-interest determination. The reversionary interest is the only structural device tying the land to the restricted use, and the same officer who applies the restriction can delete the enforcement mechanism. The appeal-standing filter at L2 is a procedural gate that distributes standing to whoever writes in by 2026-08-19 — no single actor owns a binary there — so it is the actionable deadline, not the chokepoint.

ak_consequence.sector: Industrial land / data-center siting and state development finance
ak_consequence.named_actor: DNR Commissioner (conveyance and reversion waiver); AIDEA (grantee, lessor, bond issuer)
ak_consequence.decision_or_risk: Whether ~19,950 acres of state land near Houston transfers noncompetitively into a bondable AIDEA land bank marketed for data-center-class industrial use, before any tenant, power source, water plan or site plan exists — with the reversionary interest that would claw the land back if the charitable-use premise fails available to be waived by the same officer.
ak_consequence.timeframe: Comment deadline 5:00 PM Wednesday 2026-08-19; Final Finding and Decision issues thereafter and, per the notice, issues automatically on the preliminary terms if no significant change is required.

selected_mechanism.structural_read: This is a land-assembly mechanism wearing a charitable-use statute. The tell is that AIDEA's own Deputy Director published, in the window, that there is no tenant, no power source, no cooling system, no water plan and no schedule — which is an argument for conveying land early, and simultaneously an admission that the 'public and charitable use' finding cannot rest on any specific project. AS 38.05.810(c) restricts eligible projects to uses that are 'not commercial development'; AS 44.88.080 hands the grantee power to lease on terms it 'may consider advisable' and to bond against the result. The reversionary interest in (g) is the seam between those two statutes, and (g) makes it waivable by written determination of the same officer who makes the use finding. The desk's position: the AI story here is not a data center, it is the pre-positioning of sovereign land into a financing vehicle ahead of demand, on a discretion that has no competitive test and no scored standard.
selected_mechanism.forward_implication: If you are a utility, borough, tribe, landowner, competing developer or capital allocator with any interest in Mat-Su industrial siting or Railbelt load, file a written comment with DNR DMLW LCS before 5:00 PM Wednesday 2026-08-19. That filing is the entire cost of preserving appeal rights — the notice states only timely written commenters are eligible to appeal — and after that date the Final Finding and Decision can issue on the preliminary terms without further process. Ask specifically whether the reversionary interest will be retained.
selected_mechanism.recurrence_note: Adjudicated deliberately against blocked issue #6 (2026-07-07-02 FACILITIES, ADNR state-land disposal gate / Stak Energy North Slope AI data-center lease). Same agency, and the adjacency is real. Passed as distinct on four grounds: different instrument (fee conveyance vs. lease), different statute (AS 38.05.810 charitable-use vs. general disposal), different recipient class (state public corporation vs. private developer), and a different chokepoint (a discretionary charitable-use finding plus reversion waiver, vs. a lease-approval gate). Category deliberately shifted FACILITIES to SOVEREIGNTY to reflect where the leverage actually sits. This is the desk's second DNR land mechanism in five weeks and should be the last for at least a quarter; a third would be drift regardless of statute.

The 'Alaska Data Corporation LLC / $20M / January 2026' layer was dropped (aidea.org HTTP 500; only source was an advocacy organization; AS 44.88.080's enumerated powers do not include subsidiary creation, making the claim affirmatively doubtful). The City of Houston data-center ban layer was dropped (houstonak.com returned empty, Frontiersman search 404'd; the ordinance, sponsor and 2026-08-13 vote are all unverified). Neither may appear in the post.
